entries.test: Contemporaneous studies and representative samples of internet content could establish whether low-quality service journalism and ecommerce marketing were already widespread by June 2023.
entries.note: The test concerns the substantive claim about existing internet content. The AI prediction is attributed to others; his personal lack of worry is not independently testable.

entries.test: Published content, publishers' SEO practices, and contemporaneous reporting could establish whether internet content mills were already producing substantial amounts of low-quality material designed to attract Google traffic by June 2023.
entries.note: The main assertion concerns existing content production. AI's possible contribution is a hedge, not a stated condition, and is not independently checkable.

entries.test: Archived web content and reporting on content mills could establish whether widespread production of low-quality material for search traffic had existed for years before June 2023.
entries.note: In context, 'content mill hell' refers to the previously described production of low-quality material for traffic. The reassurance and 'hell' are evaluative flourishes around that historical assertion.
